```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Oggianu L, Ottaviani M, Maddalena F, et al. PK/PD analysis of
  trazodone and gabapentin in neuropathic pain rodent models: Translational
  PK-PD modeling from nonclinical to clinical development. *Clin Transl Sci*
  2023;16(4):606-617. [doi:10.1111/cts.13472](https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13472)
  (open access via [PMC10087074](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10087074/)).
* Models:
  * `Oggianu_2023_trazodone_gabapentin_mouse` -- `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Oggianu_2023_trazodone_gabapentin_mouse"))$description`
  * `Oggianu_2023_trazodone_human` -- `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Oggianu_2023_trazodone_human"))$description`

Angelini developed a low-dose fixed combination of trazodone and gabapentin
for neuropathic pain. Oggianu and colleagues quantified the interaction of the
two drugs in the mouse acetic-acid writhing test with a sequential PK/PD
analysis, then projected the mouse PD onto human trazodone exposure to suggest
clinical starting doses.

The writhing model (Supplementary Table S1 and Figure S1) treats the
intraperitoneal acetic acid as a stimulus of amplitude `S` placed in a
compartment `a0`. The stimulus passes through nine transit compartments with a
common rate constant `ktr` into the observed writhing compartment `W`, which
empties at rate `k`. A drug removes stimulus from `a0` at a rate proportional
to its plasma concentration, `k2 * C(t)`. For the combination the loss rate is
`k2A * CA + k2B * CB + gamma * CA * CB`, so `gamma = 0` is pure additivity and
`gamma > 0` is synergy.

The paper reports several parameter sets for the drug-effect layer (Tables
3-5). The packaged mouse model uses the synergic combination fit of Table 4B,
which is the model the authors carried into the human translation. The other
sets are listed below and can be substituted with `rxode2::ini()`.

| Source | Data | k2 trazodone (L/umol/min) | k2 gabapentin (L/umol/min) | gamma | omega2 k2 (TRZ / GBP) | sigma2 add |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Table 3 | single agents | 10.9 | 0.0459 | -- | 1.42 / 1.97 | 3.20 / 2.17 |
| Table 4A | low-dose combinations, additive | 12.7 | 0.0808 | 0 | 1.43 / 1.67 | 2.62 |
| **Table 4B** (packaged) | low-dose combinations, synergic | **10.9** | **0.0490** | **16.0** | **1.42 / 1.78** | **2.64** |
| Table 5A | high-dose combinations, additive | 10.2 | 0.040 | 0 | 1.40 / 1.71 | 2.71 |
| Table 5B | high-dose combinations, synergic | 10.2 | 0.0401 | 0.0001 | 1.40 / 1.71 | 2.71 |

# Population

The mouse data come from male CD-1 mice (20-25 g). Pharmacokinetics were
measured in satellite groups of 12 fasted mice per dose with sparse sampling
to 24 h: trazodone 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg by gavage and gabapentin 10, 30 and
100 mg/kg intraperitoneally, plus the combinations 1 + 3 and 10 + 30 mg/kg
(trazodone + gabapentin) to test for a PK interaction, which was not found
(Supplementary Tables S4-S5). In the writhing test the drugs were given 1 h
before 0.7% acetic acid (16 uL/g i.p.) and writhings were counted in 5-min
bins for 30 min: trazodone 0.075-4.5 mg/kg, gabapentin 1.5-15 mg/kg, and the
combinations 0.075 + 1.5, 0.15 + 1.5, 0.5 + 5 and 1.5 + 15 mg/kg, with 6-9
mice per group.

Human trazodone PK came from a phase I four-way crossover in 23 fasted healthy
volunteers aged 22-54 years given a 50 mg immediate-release tablet and 30, 60
and 90 mg as 6% oral drops (Supplementary Table S2). Human gabapentin PK was
taken from Carlsson et al. (Ther Drug Monit 2009), whose parameters are not
reprinted in this paper.

# Mouse pharmacokinetics

Both drugs are given as a zero-order input over the fixed duration `D1`
(`rate = -2` lets the model's `dur()` apply). The model runs in minutes, so
the simulated times are converted to hours for the NCA.

```{r mouse-pk-sim}
mod_mouse <- readModelDb("Oggianu_2023_trazodone_gabapentin_mouse")

pk_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,          ~cmt,                 ~amt,
  "trazodone 1 mg/kg",  "central",            1,
  "trazodone 10 mg/kg", "central",            10,
  "gabapentin 3 mg/kg", "central_gabapentin", 3,
  "gabapentin 30 mg/kg", "central_gabapentin", 30
)
n_pk <- 200
pk_times <- c(0, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 360, 480, 720, 960, 1200, 1440)

ev_pk <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pk_groups)), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_pk + seq_len(n_pk)
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = pk_groups$amt[i], cmt = pk_groups$cmt[i],
               evid = 1, rate = -2),
    # Observations sit on the `writhing` state: with several declared
    # endpoints rxode2 needs an endpoint compartment on observation rows,
    # and every algebraic output (Cc, Cc_gabapentin) is returned anyway.
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = pk_times) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, cmt = "writhing", evid = 0, rate = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = pk_groups$treatment[i])
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230413)
sim_pk <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, ev_pk, keep = "treatment",
                                        useLinCmt = FALSE)) |>
  mutate(conc = ifelse(grepl("^trazodone", treatment), Cc, Cc_gabapentin),
         time_h = time / 60)
```

```{r mouse-pk-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated plasma concentrations in mice (median and 5th-95th percentiles of 200 simulated mice per group)."}
sim_pk |>
  filter(time_h > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time_h) |>
  summarise(med = median(conc), lo = quantile(conc, 0.05), hi = quantile(conc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time_h, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)")
```

## PKNCA

```{r mouse-pk-nca}
# Trazodone is ~30 half-lives below its peak by 24 h, where the solver
# can return values of order -1e-7 ng/mL; they are set to zero for the NCA.
conc_pk <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time_h, conc, treatment)
dose_pk <- ev_pk |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  transmute(id, time_h = time / 60, amt, treatment)

nca_pk <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_pk, conc ~ time_h | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_pk, amt ~ time_h | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
```

Supplementary Table S6 reports, for the same four dose groups, the NCA of the
observed data and the mean of the individual (post-hoc) model predictions.
The comparison uses the post-hoc means (Table S6 panels B and D).

```{r mouse-pk-compare}
published_pk <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,            ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "trazodone 1 mg/kg",     282,     220,
  "trazodone 10 mg/kg",   2156,    1509,
  "gabapentin 3 mg/kg",   3345,    9887,
  "gabapentin 30 mg/kg", 33543,   86130
)
cmp_pk <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_pk,
  reference = published_pk,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_pk, caption = attr(cmp_pk, "footnote"))
```

Gabapentin agrees with the post-hoc means within about 10%. Trazodone is
lower than the post-hoc means, by about 40-45% at 1 mg/kg and 10-30% at
10 mg/kg. That gap is in the published estimates rather than in the
simulation: for a linear model the typical AUC is `dose / (k * V1/F)`,
which is 1 / (1.25 x 5.95) = 0.134 mg h/L = 134 ng h/mL at 1 mg/kg against
the reported 220. The observed NCA (Table S6A: 219 and 1406 ng h/mL) is
itself less than dose-proportional, and the Table 1a values were fitted
jointly to 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg, so the model sits between the low and high
doses. The Table 1a values are kept as published.

```{r mouse-pk-check}
auc_typ_trz_1 <- 1000 * 1 / (1.25 * 5.95)
stopifnot(abs(auc_typ_trz_1 - 134.45) < 0.01)
gab_rows <- grepl("gabapentin", cmp_pk$treatment)
gab_pct <- as.numeric(gsub("[%*+]", "", cmp_pk[["% diff"]][gab_rows]))
stopifnot(all(abs(gab_pct) < 15))
```

# Mouse writhing model

## Control animals

The acetic acid is given at 60 min, 1 h after the (here absent) drug, as in
the experiments. It is dosed as `amt = 1` into `stimulus`; the model's
bioavailability `f(stimulus)` scales that unit dose to the animal's stimulus
amplitude `S`.

```{r pd-helpers}
n_pd <- 100
pd_times <- seq(60, 120, by = 1)

make_pd_events <- function(groups, n) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(groups)), function(i) {
    g <- groups[i, ]
    ids <- (i - 1) * n + seq_len(n)
    bind_rows(
      if (g$trz > 0) data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = g$trz, cmt = "central", evid = 1, rate = -2),
      if (g$gab > 0) data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = g$gab, cmt = "central_gabapentin", evid = 1, rate = -2),
      data.frame(id = ids, time = 60, amt = 1, cmt = "stimulus", evid = 1, rate = 0),
      tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = pd_times) |>
        mutate(amt = 0, cmt = "writhing", evid = 0, rate = 0)
    ) |>
      mutate(group = g$group)
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

pd_percentiles <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    group_by(group, time) |>
    summarise(p05 = quantile(writhing, 0.05), p50 = median(writhing),
              p95 = quantile(writhing, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
}
```

```{r pd-control, fig.cap = "Simulated writhing counts in control mice (median and 5th-95th percentiles of 100 simulated mice; model predictions without residual error)."}
ctrl <- tibble::tibble(group = "control", trz = 0, gab = 0)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230414)
sim_ctrl <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, make_pd_events(ctrl, n_pd),
                                          keep = "group", useLinCmt = FALSE))
pct_ctrl <- pd_percentiles(sim_ctrl)
ggplot(pct_ctrl, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (min; acetic acid at 60 min)", y = "Number of writhings")
```

With the typical values the control curve can be checked against the
structure directly: the stimulus leaves `a0` at `ktr`, and the writhing count
peaks about ten minutes after the injection.

```{r pd-control-check}
ev_typ <- make_pd_events(ctrl, 1)
sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, ev_typ, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
                                         useLinCmt = FALSE))
t_peak <- sim_typ$time[which.max(sim_typ$writhing)] - 60
w_peak <- max(sim_typ$writhing)
c(t_peak_min = t_peak, peak_writhings = round(w_peak, 2))
# A total stimulus S passes through the chain, so the area under W over all
# time is S / k. The 60-minute grid captures nearly all of it.
auc_w <- sum(diff(sim_typ$time) * (head(sim_typ$writhing, -1) + tail(sim_typ$writhing, -1)) / 2)
stopifnot(t_peak >= 9, t_peak <= 12, abs(auc_w / (26.10 / 0.104) - 1) < 0.05)
```

## Replication of Figure 1: combinations under additivity

Figure 1 simulates 100 mice for each combination group assuming additivity.
The single-agent potencies of Table 3 are used here with `gamma = 0`.

```{r fig1, message = FALSE, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Oggianu 2023: simulated writhings (5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of 100 mice) for the four combinations under additivity, using the Table 3 single-agent potencies."}
mod_additive_t3 <- mod_mouse |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lslope = log(10.9), lslope_gabapentin = log(0.0459), synergy = 0,
    etalslope ~ 1.42, etalslope_gabapentin ~ 1.97
  )
combos <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,                                  ~trz,  ~gab,
  "(a) 0.075 mg/kg TRZ + 1.5 mg/kg GBP",  0.075,  1.5,
  "(b) 0.15 mg/kg TRZ + 1.5 mg/kg GBP",   0.15,   1.5,
  "(c) 0.5 mg/kg TRZ + 5 mg/kg GBP",      0.5,    5,
  "(d) 1.5 mg/kg TRZ + 15 mg/kg GBP",     1.5,    15
)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230415)
sim_fig1 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_additive_t3, make_pd_events(combos, n_pd),
                                          keep = "group", useLinCmt = FALSE))
pct_fig1 <- pd_percentiles(sim_fig1)
ggplot(pct_fig1, aes(time)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), colour = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Number of writhings")
```

The published panels peak near 70 min with a median of roughly 12, 11, 6.5
and 3 writhings for panels (a)-(d) and a 95th percentile of roughly 17, 18,
14 and 10 (read from the figure by the maintainers). The simulated peak
percentiles are:

```{r fig1-table}
fig1_peak <- pct_fig1 |>
  group_by(group) |>
  slice_max(p50, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(figure_p50 = c(12, 11, 6.5, 3), figure_p95 = c(17, 18, 14, 10))
fig1_peak |>
  transmute(
    "Group" = group,
    "Peak time (min)" = time,
    "Simulated 5th" = round(p05, 1),
    "Simulated median" = round(p50, 1),
    "Figure 1 median (approx.)" = figure_p50,
    "Simulated 95th" = round(p95, 1),
    "Figure 1 95th (approx.)" = figure_p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
# Structural check: the higher-dose combinations suppress writhing more.
stopifnot(
  fig1_peak$p50[3] < fig1_peak$p50[1],
  fig1_peak$p50[4] < fig1_peak$p50[3]
)
```

The simulated peak medians and 95th percentiles fall within about 1.5
writhings of the published panels.

## Additive versus synergic fits (Tables 4 and 5)

For the two low-dose combinations the synergic model (Table 4B, the packaged
parameters) lowered the objective function by 17 points relative to the
additive model (Table 4A). The typical-value writhing areas over the 30-min
counting window show what `gamma` adds:

```{r synergy, message = FALSE}
mod_additive_t4a <- mod_mouse |>
  rxode2::ini(lslope = log(12.7), lslope_gabapentin = log(0.0808), synergy = 0)
mod_additive_t5a <- mod_mouse |>
  rxode2::ini(lslope = log(10.2), lslope_gabapentin = log(0.040), synergy = 0)
low_high <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,                                ~trz,   ~gab,
  "control",                             0,      0,
  "0.075 mg/kg TRZ + 1.5 mg/kg GBP",    0.075,  1.5,
  "0.15 mg/kg TRZ + 1.5 mg/kg GBP",     0.15,   1.5,
  "0.5 mg/kg TRZ + 5 mg/kg GBP",        0.5,    5,
  "1.5 mg/kg TRZ + 15 mg/kg GBP",       1.5,    15
)
ev_lh <- make_pd_events(low_high, 1) |> filter(time <= 90)
w_area <- function(m) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev_lh, omega = NA, sigma = NA, keep = "group",
                                useLinCmt = FALSE)) |>
    group_by(group) |>
    summarise(area = sum(diff(time) * (head(writhing, -1) + tail(writhing, -1)) / 2),
              .groups = "drop")
}
syn_tab <- w_area(mod_mouse) |>
  rename(synergic_4B = area) |>
  left_join(rename(w_area(mod_additive_t4a), additive_4A = area), by = "group") |>
  left_join(rename(w_area(mod_additive_t5a), additive_5A = area), by = "group")
ctrl_area <- syn_tab$synergic_4B[syn_tab$group == "control"]
syn_tab |>
  mutate(across(-group, ~ round(100 * (1 - .x / ctrl_area), 1))) |>
  filter(group != "control") |>
  rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "% inhibition, synergic (Table 4B)" = synergic_4B,
    "% inhibition, additive (Table 4A)" = additive_4A,
    "% inhibition, additive (Table 5A)" = additive_5A
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The synergy estimate comes from the two low-dose combinations only. At the
high-dose combinations the authors found `gamma` indistinguishable from zero
(Table 5B, `gamma = 0.0001`), so the packaged `gamma = 16` overstates the
interaction there; use `rxode2::ini(mod, synergy = 0)` with the Table 5
potencies for doses at or above 0.5 + 5 mg/kg.

# Human trazodone

## Pharmacokinetics (Supplementary Table S3)

Table S3 reports the simulated AUC from time zero to infinity after single
oral trazodone doses of 0.5-50 mg, and the same AUC rescaled for protein
binding (`AUCeq`).

```{r human-pk}
mod_human <- readModelDb("Oggianu_2023_trazodone_human")
hum_doses <- c(0.5, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50)
n_hum <- 200
hum_times <- c(0, 0.083, 0.167, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72)
ev_hum <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(hum_doses), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_hum + seq_len(n_hum)
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = hum_doses[i], cmt = "depot", evid = 1),
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = hum_times) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, cmt = "central", evid = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(hum_doses[i], "mg"))
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230416)
sim_hum <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human, ev_hum, keep = "treatment"))

nca_hum <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(filter(sim_hum, !is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(filter(ev_hum, evid == 1), amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
published_hum <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = paste(hum_doses, "mg"),
  aucinf.obs = c(46.1, 92.7, 458, 931, 2323, 4643)
)
cmp_hum <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_hum,
  reference = published_hum,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_hum, caption = attr(cmp_hum, "footnote"))
```

The reference values are the Table S3 medians. The typical-value AUC is
`dose / (CL/F)` = 50.7 ng h/mL at 0.5 mg, about 10% above the published
median of 46.1; the published simulation's median-to-dose ratio is constant
across doses (92.2-92.9 ng h/mL per mg), so the gap is a fixed scale offset
rather than nonlinearity. The `AUCeq` column of Table S3 is `AUC x (1 - 0.97)
/ (1 - 0.89)`, the same factor the model applies before the concentration
drives the writhing layer:

```{r human-pk-check}
fu_ratio <- (1 - 0.97) / (1 - 0.89)
table_s3 <- tibble::tibble(
  dose = hum_doses,
  auc_tot_mean = c(48.1, 96.3, 481, 967, 2438, 4784),
  auc_eq_mean = c(13.1, 26.3, 131, 264, 665, 1305)
)
table_s3 |>
  mutate(ratio = round(auc_eq_mean / auc_tot_mean, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(all(abs(table_s3$auc_eq_mean / table_s3$auc_tot_mean - fu_ratio) < 0.003))
hum_pct <- as.numeric(gsub("[%*+]", "", cmp_hum[["% diff"]]))
stopifnot(abs(median(hum_pct)) < 15)
```

## Translation of the writhing effect (Table 6, trazodone alone)

The paper's design is replicated for each virtual subject: the stimulus is
first applied without drug, the compartments are reset (`evid = 3`), and the
stimulus is applied again 1 h after a trazodone dose. Percent inhibition is
one minus the ratio of the two writhing areas over the 30-min counting
window. Both phases share the subject's parameters, so the comparison is
within subject, as in the paper.

```{r human-translation}
grid_30 <- seq(0, 0.5, by = 1 / 120)
ev_tr <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(hum_doses), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_hum + seq_len(n_hum)
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = 1, cmt = "stimulus", evid = 1),
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = grid_30) |> mutate(amt = 0, cmt = "writhing", evid = 0),
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 24, amt = 0, cmt = "writhing", evid = 3),
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 24, amt = hum_doses[i], cmt = "depot", evid = 1),
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 25, amt = 1, cmt = "stimulus", evid = 1),
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = 25 + grid_30) |> mutate(amt = 0, cmt = "writhing", evid = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(dose = hum_doses[i])
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230417)
sim_tr <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human, ev_tr, keep = "dose"))
inh <- sim_tr |>
  mutate(phase = ifelse(time < 24, "no_drug", "drug")) |>
  group_by(id, dose, phase) |>
  summarise(area = sum(diff(time) * (head(writhing, -1) + tail(writhing, -1)) / 2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = phase, values_from = area) |>
  mutate(pct_inh = 100 * (1 - drug / no_drug))

table6 <- tibble::tibble(
  dose = hum_doses,
  paper_mean = c(4.93, 9.20, 27.6, 37.5, 56.2, 69.41),
  paper_median = c(2.76, 5.67, 21.7, 34.1, 58.7, 73.96),
  paper_q1 = c(1.18, 2.50, 10.5, 18.6, 38.4, 55.09),
  paper_q3 = c(6.03, 11.75, 39.6, 53.3, 75.0, 85.97)
)
inh_sum <- inh |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(sim_mean = mean(pct_inh), sim_median = median(pct_inh),
            sim_q1 = quantile(pct_inh, 0.25), sim_q3 = quantile(pct_inh, 0.75)) |>
  left_join(table6, by = "dose")
inh_sum |>
  transmute(
    "Trazodone dose (mg)" = dose,
    "Mean, paper" = paper_mean, "Mean, simulated" = round(sim_mean, 1),
    "Median, paper" = paper_median, "Median, simulated" = round(sim_median, 1),
    "Q1, paper" = paper_q1, "Q1, simulated" = round(sim_q1, 1),
    "Q3, paper" = paper_q3, "Q3, simulated" = round(sim_q3, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Percent inhibition of the pain stimulus after single oral trazodone doses (Table 6, gabapentin 0 mg column).")
```

```{r human-translation-check}
# Centre-of-distribution checks across the six doses. With a 119% CV on the
# potency, a 200-subject mean moves by several points between cohorts, so
# the check is on the median difference across doses, not on any one dose.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(inh_sum$sim_median - inh_sum$paper_median)) < 4,
  abs(median(inh_sum$sim_mean - inh_sum$paper_mean)) < 4
)
```

```{r human-translation-plot, fig.cap = "Percent inhibition of the writhing stimulus versus human trazodone dose: simulated median and interquartile range (line and band) against the Table 6 values (points and error bars)."}
ggplot(inh_sum, aes(dose)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = sim_q1, ymax = sim_q3), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim_median)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(y = paper_median, ymin = paper_q1, ymax = paper_q3), colour = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Trazodone dose (mg)", y = "Inhibition of writhing stimulus (%)")
```

The gabapentin columns of Table 6 (gabapentin alone and with trazodone) need
the human gabapentin model of Carlsson et al. (2009), which this paper uses
but does not reprint, so they are not reproduced here.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Time units.** The mouse model runs in minutes because the writhing
  parameters are per minute; the mouse PK parameters keep their published
  hour units in `ini()` and are divided by 60 in `model()`. The human model
  runs in hours and multiplies the per-minute writhing parameters by 60.
* **Molar conversion.** The potencies `k2` are per umol/L, so the plasma
  concentration is divided by the free-base molecular weight (trazodone
  371.86, gabapentin 171.24 g/mol). The molecular weights are not printed in
  the paper. The Table 6 reproduction above depends on this conversion and
  agrees with the published values.
* **Stimulus as a dose.** The paper gives the stimulus as the initial
  condition `a0(0) = S`. Because the drugs are given 1 h earlier, the model
  doses the stimulus as `amt = 1` into `stimulus` at the time of the acetic
  acid, with `f(stimulus) = S`.
* **Number of transit compartments.** Table 2 reports `n = 9` with an
  interindividual variance (`omega2 n = 0.00848`). The PK/PD equations of
  Supplementary Table S1B write the chain as nine explicit compartments, and
  an explicit chain cannot carry a random number of compartments, so the
  model follows the printed equations with `n = 9` for every animal and omits
  `omega2 n`.
* **Packaged drug-effect parameters.** The mouse model carries the Table 4B
  synergic fit. It was estimated on the two low-dose combinations; at the
  high-dose combinations the authors found additivity (Table 5). The Table 3
  single-agent fits had separate additive residual variances (3.20 and 2.17);
  the model carries the single Table 4B value (2.64).
* **Sequential estimation.** The PK parameters and the control-group PD
  parameters were estimated first and held fixed while the potencies and
  `gamma` were estimated. They are not wrapped in `fixed()`, because they are
  estimates from this paper. The zero-order input durations `D1` (5 and
  10 min) have no reported standard error and are encoded as fixed.
* **Human translation.** The writhing parameters in the human model are the
  mouse estimates and are wrapped in `fixed()`; the trazodone potency is
  assumed equal across species, as the paper states. Human concentrations
  are scaled by the unbound-fraction ratio (1 - 0.97) / (1 - 0.89) before
  they act. The per-subject percent inhibition uses the 30-min counting
  window of the mouse experiment; the paper does not state the window used
  for the human areas, and integrating the full writhing curve instead
  changes the percentages by a fraction of a percentage point.
* **Trazodone mouse exposure.** The typical-value trazodone AUC and Cmax are
  below the post-hoc means of Table S6 (see the PKNCA section); the Table 1a
  values are used as published.
* **Human gabapentin.** The human gabapentin PK model (Carlsson et al., Ther
  Drug Monit 2009;31:86-94) is cited but not reprinted, so the human model
  covers trazodone only.
* **Animal numbers.** The total number of mice in the writhing experiments is
  not reported (6-9 per group), so `n_subjects` is `NA` in the mouse model.
